title: Six thousand words
summary: The broadsheet writer wants a long interview: your childhood, your family, the bad bits. How much you give him decides what the country reads. A season on, the piece wins a prize, or it doesn't exist.

ends.title: The piece
ends.text: You told a writer the truth about where you came from. Your dad has it framed.

ends.title: Stock answers
ends.text: You gave him the usual. He wrote six hundred words instead of six thousand.

beats.title: The long read

event.title: The long read
event.speaker: broadsheet
setup: {broadsheet.name} from the {broadsheet.outlet} has bought you a coffee and put his phone on the table to record. He's read everything ever written about you.

say: "Not football. I want the estate, your dad working nights, the academy letter. The bits nobody's asked about."

replies.label: Tell him about your dad working nights.
"Hard work, a great family, the gaffer believed in me."

say: He doesn't write anything. He just lets you talk. After an hour he says, "Can I use the bit about the boots he bought you with his overtime?"

open.text: Six thousand words on a Saturday. Your dad reads it four times and doesn't ring you, and then he rings you.

asked.text: You ring your dad from the café toilet. He's quiet for a while. "Go on, then."

usual.text: He writes it down, politely, and switches the phone off after twenty minutes.

beats.hint: A writer wants a proper interview

beats.title: The prize

event.title: The prize
event.speaker: broadsheet
setup: {if arc.path=='open'}A season on. {broadsheet.short} texts: the piece about you has won sports feature of the year. He wants you and your dad at the dinner.{/if}
{if arc.path=='usual'}A season on. {broadsheet.short} has written a long piece about a team-mate of yours instead. Everyone's talking about it.{/if}

choices.label: {if arc.path=='open'}Take your dad to the dinner.{/if}{if arc.path=='usual'}Read it.{/if}

outcomes.text: Your dad wears a suit for the first time since your nan's funeral. He tells the man from the next table about the overtime.
It's very good. You read it twice.
Your dad goes on his own and brings you back the menu.

beats.hint: A season on, the writer gets in touch
